paragraph: In November 2019 the Irene Neto Maternity Hospital in Lubango ran an electronic obstetric record prototype that [was part of a doctoral research project at the University of Beira Interior, Portugal](<http://www.academicstar.us/UploadFile/Picture/2020-7/2020716175015266.pdf>). The prototype was [in its test phase](<http://www.academicstar.us/UploadFile/Picture/2020-7/2020716175015266.pdf>). Between March and September 2019, two Luanda tuberculosis facilities [kept clinical and surveillance data entirely on paper records and registers](<https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/public-health/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2022.745928/full>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found is dated after 2019. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

GEPE, the health ministry's Office of Studies, Planning and Statistics, [oversees the health information system and has been moving it onto DHIS2 since 2015](<https://doi.org/10.5937/smclk6-58193>), a June 2025 article states. Health facilities report on paper. Municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into DHIS2. In the last twelve months, in March 2026, a WHO Angola and HISP UiO mission assessed the platform. The ministry and its partners [agreed to build dashboards for decision-makers and train staff at all levels](<https://dhis2.org/pt-pt/angola-to-partner-with-hisp-uio-and-who/>). No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

[Forty-one of 71 public and faith-based hospitals are computerised](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099050923073520082/pdf/P17512808c1cbf01009a830d30eb4cb8732.pdf>), patient health records included, the World Bank reported in March 2023. Thirty-nine of them run OpenClinic. The hospitals are not interconnected, and each has its own patient identifier. [Six health centres are computerised under a pilot financed by Enabel](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099050923073520082/pdf/P17512808c1cbf01009a830d30eb4cb8732.pdf>), the same report says. In the last twelve months, a memorandum signed on 6 February 2026 [commits Burundi to roll SIDAinfo out in 460 facilities by 2026 and 572 by 2028](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/BURUNDI_FL-2026-00021_August-2026-Production_RELEASE.pdf>). Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

Burundi's health ministry [collected its 2023 data through the national DHIS2 platform](<https://extranet.who.int/uhcpartnershiplivemonitoring/system/files/doc_attachments/Annuaire%20des%20Statistiques%20Sanitaires%202023.pdf>) from health centres, district hospitals and national hospitals. Its yearbook of July 2024 states this. The World Bank reported in March 2023 that [the entry into DHIS2 is made at the facility](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099050923073520082/pdf/P17512808c1cbf01009a830d30eb4cb8732.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a [memorandum of 6 February 2026](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/BURUNDI_FL-2026-00021_August-2026-Production_RELEASE.pdf>) with the United States provided support for linking DHIS2 with SIDAinfo and other systems, to 31 December 2030. No share or count of health centres keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

No stage is set. No source found, as at 13 October 2026, states a tier, a place of digitisation or a clinic count for electronic patient records in Benin. A digital health booklet is held only as a pledge. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

Benin's health ministry [adopted DHIS2 from 2014](<https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/front-office-resources/production/uploads/publication/attachment/46e5f76a-5f8f-4780-9d32-d51df5c239c2/02be6fdb-3d72-4984-adba-f696163051fd.pdf>), its 2022 statistical yearbook says. In 2022 a facility in every zone sanitaire [sent its paper report to the zone before the 5th of each month](<https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/front-office-resources/production/uploads/publication/attachment/46e5f76a-5f8f-4780-9d32-d51df5c239c2/02be6fdb-3d72-4984-adba-f696163051fd.pdf>), and the zone keyed it into DHIS2. No dated event has been found in the last twelve months. No number or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found, and no tier below the health centre is named. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

NetAfrique reported on 18 July 2025 that OpenClinic, a hospital management system with clinical and nursing records, [is deployed at pilot sites, the CHUR of Ouahigouya and the CHR of Manga](<https://netafrique.net/digitalisation-de-la-gestion-des-hopitaux-au-burkina-des-administrateurs-en-formation-dans-la-region-du-nazinon/>). At Manga the 2024-2025 pilot [ended in full digitisation of admissions](<https://doi.org/10.3233/shti260468>). By April 2023 a study found [the public health system lacked computerised patient records](<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12911-024-02574-4>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The position at primary clinics has not been found. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts, with each record staying in the facility that made it.

The Ministry of Health's Direction générale des études et des statistiques sectorielles [coordinates the national health information system](<https://www.sante.gov.bf/fileadmin/manuel_procedure_gestion_info_sanitaire_avril_2025.pdf>), its manual of July 2023 sets. In 2024 [health facilities sent their monthly reports to the district](<https://www.wakatsera.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/annuaire-statistique-2024-du-ministere-burkinabe-de-la-Sante.pdf>), where data managers keyed them into Endos-BF. In districts with decentralised entry, [the heads of health facilities entered their own monthly activity reports](<https://www.wakatsera.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/annuaire-statistique-2024-du-ministere-burkinabe-de-la-Sante.pdf>). In the last twelve months, Enabel reported training at Dédougou and Tenkodogo in July 2026. The [training included quality control of DHIS2 data](<https://open.enabel.be/en/BFA/2798/3690/u/analyse-et-utilisation-des-donnees-sanitaires-les-districts-de-dedougou-et-de-tenkodogo-renforcent-leurs-capacites-pour-mieux-decider-et-mieux-agir.html>). No number or share of primary clinics keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

The Ministry of Health's budget speech of 5 March 2026 states that [it and the Ministry of Local Government and Traditional Affairs will roll out the completed EMR](<https://www.botswanaspeaks.gov.bw/media/COMMITTEE%20OF%20SUPPPLY%20SPEECHES/HEALTH-Committee%20of%20Supply%20Speech%20-%20FINAL%2004-03-2026%20Vol%20I.pdf>). It covers the remaining 29 districts in 2026/27. In the last twelve months, on 5 March 2026, the Assistant Minister told Parliament that [Phase 1 of the ministry's centralised Electronic Medical Record had been implemented](<https://www.botswanaspeaks.gov.bw/media/COMMITTEE%20OF%20SUPPPLY%20SPEECHES/HEALTH-Committee%20of%20Supply%20Speech%20-%20FINAL%2004-03-2026%20Vol%20I.pdf>), covering [22 health facilities in Ngami](<https://www.botswanaspeaks.gov.bw/media/COMMITTEE%20OF%20SUPPPLY%20SPEECHES/HEALTH-Committee%20of%20Supply%20Speech%20-%20FINAL%2004-03-2026%20Vol%20I.pdf>). On 19 November 2025 the Minister of Local Government had said [the Electronic Medical Records system was being piloted in two districts](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/89169>). No source shows a unique patient identifier in use. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

WHO's country office report for 2024-2025 describes DHIS2 as [the Government's selected "gold standard" platform for aggregate data](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2026-05/WHO%20Botswana%20Biennial%20Report%202024-2025_web.pdf>). The same report [lists facilities' heavy reliance on paper-based reporting as a challenge](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2026-05/WHO%20Botswana%20Biennial%20Report%202024-2025_web.pdf>). MEASURE Evaluation gives [100% of public health facilities as reporting through DHIS2](<https://www.measureevaluation.org/his-strengthening-resource-center/country-profiles-1/botswana.html>) for 2016 to 2018. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source gives the level at which paper reports are keyed, and no share or count of clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

HISP Rwanda reported on 18 March 2026 that it [is supporting deployment of the HISP EMR](<https://hisprwanda.org/hisp-emr-digitizing-hospital-care-in-the-central-african-republic/>), known in the country as e-SENI. In the last twelve months, the report describes [a phased deployment under way](<https://hisprwanda.org/hisp-emr-digitizing-hospital-care-in-the-central-african-republic/>). It covers site assessments, configuration in French and staff training. It states that [medical records in many facilities are still kept in paper registers](<https://hisprwanda.org/hisp-emr-digitizing-hospital-care-in-the-central-african-republic/>). No source found gives the number of e-SENI sites or any clinics figure. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

A DHIS2 Community poster of May 2026 says the ministry [undertook the reform of the national health information system (SNIS) and adopted DHIS2 as the national platform](<https://community.dhis2.org/t/dhis2-pour-la-reconstruction-du-snis-cas-de-la-rca/72669>). By 2025 DHIS2 [had been deployed in all 35 health districts, with data managers recruited and offline and VSAT connections](<https://community.dhis2.org/t/dhis2-pour-la-reconstruction-du-snis-cas-de-la-rca/72669>). The IMPULSE study assessed 14 facilities chosen for access and security, on data to July 2024. It found that [21.4% of them used a functional electronic system for routine data entry](<https://jogh.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/jogh-15-04295n.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows primary clinics entering their own reports. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

The health ministry's digital health directorate [deployed its patient record, the DPI, in August 2024](<https://disd.ci/deploiement-reussi-du-dossier-patient-informatise-a-lhg-de-ferkessedougou-une-etape-cruciale-vers-la-digitalisation-des-soins/>). In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the directorate's officials said [258 health facilities use it](<https://digitalmag.ci/sante-numerique-vers-une-interoperabilite-dans-le-systeme-de-sante-en-cote-divoire/>), without giving their type. On 4 September 2026 a national workshop [named the patient record among ten quick wins due by the end of 2026](<https://afriksoir.net/transformation-numerique-les-travaux-retiennent-59-services-prioritaires-et-dix-quick-wins-attendus-pour-la-fin-2026/>). No source found shows primary clinics using the record, as against having it deployed. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

The health ministry's annual report for 2020 [calls DHIS2 the national database of routine data](<https://www.snisdiis.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Rapport-Annuel-sur-la-Situation-Sanitaire-RASS-2020-VF.pdf>). In 2020 each first-contact establishment drew up a monthly report from its registers. The district's surveillance officer keyed it into DHIS2 [at the departmental health directorate](<https://www.snisdiis.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Rapport-Annuel-sur-la-Situation-Sanitaire-RASS-2020-VF.pdf>). By the ministry's account, [first-contact establishments did not enter their own reports](<https://www.snisdiis.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/Rapport-Annuel-sur-la-Situation-Sanitaire-RASS-2020-VF.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found after 2022 says where clinics' reports are keyed. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

The Ministry of Public Health's electronic medical record, the DME, runs on Bahmni. Its plan for 2026 to 2030 states that [the record was deployed in about fifty pilot health facilities during the 2020-2024 plan](<https://www.minsante.cm/site/sites/default/files/PSNSN%202026-2030%20Fr.pdf>). The plan [budgets for 2026 the selection of a partner and a public-private partnership contract to deploy one](<https://www.minsante.cm/site/sites/default/files/PSNSN%202026-2030%20Fr.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the SmartMobileClinic project ran [12 rural campaigns between November 2025 and January 2026](<https://diasporafordevelopment.eu/cpt_actions/smartmobileclinic-expanding-telehealth-services-in-rural-communities-in-cameroon/>). The level of the pilot facilities has not been found. Routine use at any hospital has not been shown. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

The ministry's DHIS2 plan of April 2022 states that [a nationwide HMIS is in place for aggregate data](<https://biblio-minsante.cm/server/api/core/bitstreams/7f4eeb8b-67fe-4692-b639-3c43e8a3580c/content>). Data entry is at the facility level. The family health directorate gives [completeness of monthly activity reports in DHIS2 as 96% nationally for October to December 2025](<https://biblio-minsante.cm/server/api/core/bitstreams/2bc60008-7482-4a7c-842d-15f112a2efd7/content>). In the last twelve months, the ministry [published its digital health plan for 2026 to 2030 in March 2026](<https://www.minsante.cm/site/sites/default/files/PSNSN%202026-2030%20Fr.pdf>). The 96% measures reports received. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

The national agency ANICNS [leads the health-sector digital transformation project](<https://actualite.cd/2024/11/23/rdc-lanicns-dote-les-hopitaux-de-mbuji-mayi-et-kalemie-dequipements-numeriques-pour-leur>), Actualite.cd reported on 23 November 2024. On 12 July 2024 it [handed digital kits and three hospital information systems to three sites in Kinshasa](<https://actualite.cd/2024/07/13/kinshasa-lanicns-dote-trois-etablissements-hospitaliers-de-kits-medicaux-digitalises>). In the last twelve months, on 16 June 2026, it [opened a call for the now-mandatory approval of hospital information systems](<https://www.congoquotidien.com/2026/06/16/actualite-rdc-homologation-sih-rdc/>). Each system is [to include a complete computerised patient record](<https://www.congoquotidien.com/2026/06/16/actualite-rdc-homologation-sih-rdc/>). A survey of seven Kananga hospitals in 2023 [found 4.7% of 86 staff managing patient information electronically](<https://www.scirp.net/journal/paperinformation?paperid=136674>). No source found states that any facility uses an electronic patient record. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

DHIS2.org in December 2025 calls the national DHIS2 [locally owned and managed infrastructure of the Ministry of Health](<https://dhis2.org/drc-ebola-response-2025/>). The ministry's report of 14 August 2022 states that [12,050 of the 16,010 health facilities listed in DHIS2 report in it](<https://www.countdown2030.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Rapport-technique-actualise-RDC_Atelier-danalyse-donnees-SRMNEA-Nut_14.08.2022.pdf>). A HISP evaluation in late 2021 found that [facilities send paper reports to the zone office for DHIS2 entry](<https://dhis2.org/drc-data-use/>). The HIV Insight Dashboard is built inside the national DHIS2. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, [Lualaba became the first province to make it its primary tool for provincial data validation](<https://icap.columbia.edu/news-events/icaps-hiv-insight-dashboard-streamlines-data-analysis-in-the-democratic-republic-of-congo/>). No share or count of facilities entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

No stage is set. Nothing found, as at 30 September 2026, says whether patient records are kept on paper or digitally at any tier. A public hospital's organisation decree names a hospital information system, without saying that it holds the clinical record. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

The health ministry's national health development plan for 2023 to 2026, published in September 2024, [names DHIS2 as the principal platform for collecting and processing health information](<https://sante.gouv.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/PLAN-NATIONAL-DE-DEVELOPPEMENT-SANITAIRE-DU-CONGO-2023-2026_VERSION-OFFICIELLE.pdf>). It states that nearly all facilities compile their reports on paper and [send them to the health districts for entry](<https://sante.gouv.cg/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/PLAN-NATIONAL-DE-DEVELOPPEMENT-SANITAIRE-DU-CONGO-2023-2026_VERSION-OFFICIELLE.pdf>). No change dated within the last twelve months has been found. WHO's annual report for 2025 says [401 data collectors were equipped for electronic transmission of data](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2026-04/Rapport%20Annuel%202025%20OMS_Congo.pdf>), without naming their tier. No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

In July 2021 the Ministry of Health stated in its digital health strategy that [the electronic patient record does not exist in the country](<https://extranet.who.int/cpcd/sites/default/files/public_file_repository/com_comoros_strategie-nationale-de-sant-numerique_2022-2026.pdf>). The strategy [plans a modular application for reception, consultations, tests, hospitalisation and billing](<https://extranet.who.int/cpcd/sites/default/files/public_file_repository/com_comoros_strategie-nationale-de-sant-numerique_2022-2026.pdf>). The World Bank [recorded a hospital management information system as not functional at 31 August 2024](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099111924122078581/pdf/P175840-1a3a0438-2d5c-487f-8960-7e60d83dfb5b.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated after July 2021 confirms or replaces the ministry's statement. Preparing would need electronic patient records in use in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system procured or being prepared, with primary clinics not using them beyond pilot sites.

WHO Comoros reports that [DHIS2 was extended to all 91 public-level health structures in 2025](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2026-05/OMS%20Comores%20_%20Rapport%20annuel%20des%20r%C3%A9sultats%202025%20%20PUBLICATION.pdf>). The Ministry of Health's strategy of July 2021 describes the earlier national system as [semi-electronic and computerised at the level of the regions](<https://extranet.who.int/cpcd/sites/default/files/public_file_repository/com_comoros_strategie-nationale-de-sant-numerique_2022-2026.pdf>). DHIS2 states that [almost 99% of all public health facilities used DHIS2 for health service reporting in 2024](<https://dhis2.org/supply-chain-management-dhis2-open-msupply-comoros/>). No event dated within the last twelve months has been found. No source found says where DHIS2 reports are keyed, and the 99% counts all public facilities. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility, on a published share or count of primary clinics.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference of February 2024 [name Medicine One as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Terms%2Bof%2BReference%2B-ugpe.pdf/b0d39856-c19f-5ca9-2081-a9cdeb683c0a?t=1706880078938>). As at February 2024 it was [in use only in Praia's health facilities, namely its health centres and the central hospital](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Terms%2Bof%2BReference%2B-ugpe.pdf/b0d39856-c19f-5ca9-2081-a9cdeb683c0a?t=1706880078938>). In the last twelve months, on 18 December 2025, the Minister of Health said [each citizen will get a unique patient code giving access to a digital clinical history](<https://www.balai.cv/noticias/ministro-da-saude-aponta-avanco-da-digitalizacao-do-sistema-nacional-de-saude/>). No count of sites or share of primary clinics has been found. The patient code is not shown in use. Establishing would need patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

The Ministry of Health's terms of reference of February 2024 [name DHIS-2 as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Terms%2Bof%2BReference%2B-ugpe.pdf/b0d39856-c19f-5ca9-2081-a9cdeb683c0a?t=1706880078938>). They state that it is [in operation in all structures of the national health service](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Terms%2Bof%2BReference%2B-ugpe.pdf/b0d39856-c19f-5ca9-2081-a9cdeb683c0a?t=1706880078938>). The structures include [32 health centres, 34 health posts and 114 basic health units](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/documents/20126/0/Terms%2Bof%2BReference%2B-ugpe.pdf/b0d39856-c19f-5ca9-2081-a9cdeb683c0a?t=1706880078938>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Nothing found says who keys them. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

No stage is set. A report of 2024 describes medical follow-up on paper, and names no tier and no system. No electronic medical record is named at any tier. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a dated source stating that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

UNFPA Djibouti reported on a workshop dated 2 February 2025 that the Ministry of Health [ensures national governance of the integrated DHIS2 and GBVIMS-Health platform](<https://djibouti.unfpa.org/en/news/strengthening-governance-gender-based-violence-data-integrating-gbvims-health-dhis2-djibouti>). The World Bank records [84% of all health facilities with DHIS-2 data entry at the facility level at 30 June 2025, against an end target of 65% for May 2027](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102225172035856/pdf/P178033-79193a4a-bd86-4d36-b863-cdbc43bde6c7.pdf>). Its [baseline was 35% in May 2022](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102225172035856/pdf/P178033-79193a4a-bd86-4d36-b863-cdbc43bde6c7.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The 84% is of all health facilities, with no numerator or denominator. No share or count of primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published count showing more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports.

From 2018 the ministry [put an earlier record, DEMDZ, into certain pilot hospitals](<https://dspace.univ-mila.dz/jspui/bitstream/123456789/1787/1/690-Texte%20de%20l%27article-2080-1-10-20220611.pdf>). In July 2026 it [launched a national deployment plan aiming at over 2,500 health structures in all 69 wilayas](<https://interlignes.dz/sante-lancement-du-deploiement-du-dossier-medical-electronique-a-travers-les-69-wilayas/>). In the last twelve months, El Watan reported in September 2026 that the record [was under way in several pilot facilities, with 15 November 2026 set as the deadline for all public health establishments](<https://elwatan.dz/sante-alger-fixe-au-15-novembre-lecheance-finale-pour-la-numerisation-totale-des-hopitaux/>). [Annaba's El Bouni primary-care facility trained staff for the record going live on 15 November 2026](<https://algerieconfluences.dz/des-le-15-novembre-annaba-passe-au-dossier-medical-electronique/>). No count or share of hospitals or primary clinics using the record has been found. No source states where it is keyed. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

The Ministry of Health, with WHO support, [began training health practitioners and IT staff to use the DHIS2 platform](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2024-09/1%20OMS%20ALGERIE%20RAPPORT%20BIENNAL%202022%202023.pdf%20%287%29.pdf>), the WHO Algeria office reports. The first session [ran for five days in December 2023, led by an international expert](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2024-09/1%20OMS%20ALGERIE%20RAPPORT%20BIENNAL%202022%202023.pdf%20%287%29.pdf>). It [trained a first team of 20 health practitioners and IT staff](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2024-09/1%20OMS%20ALGERIE%20RAPPORT%20BIENNAL%202022%202023.pdf%20%287%29.pdf>). The national digital health strategy [was still a draft in November 2023](<https://afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2024-09/1%20OMS%20ALGERIE%20RAPPORT%20BIENNAL%202022%202023.pdf%20%287%29.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no use of the platform after the first training has been found. Establishing would need a national system that takes the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from paper forms, with a minority of primary clinics entering their own or no figure published.

The National Health Compact of December 2025 [put electronic health records at early pilots](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/0273f33ab6ee48c5d842108b9b55c789-0140022025/related/HealthCompacts-EGYPT.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Egypt Healthcare Authority's head said in July 2026 that [its health information system runs in 265 primary care centres and units](<https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/4321204>). They are in the six first-phase insurance governorates. [On 9 November 2026 the Authority's chairman said a unified platform lets patients be treated in any governorate it covers](<https://cairoict.com/news/from-digital-records-to-home-grown-medical-ai>). It held about 6.2 million electronic health files. No national share of primary clinics has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic patient records, entered at the point of care and retrievable at another facility.

Egypt's answers to the WHO EMRO civil registration questionnaire, published in 2025, describe [the Ministry of Health's national health information system](<https://www.emro.who.int/images/stories/crvs/documents/egypt.pdf>). Health offices notify births and deaths. [Copies go to the health department at district level](<https://www.emro.who.int/images/stories/crvs/documents/egypt.pdf>). The district department [processes the notifications electronically into the national system](<https://www.emro.who.int/images/stories/crvs/documents/egypt.pdf>). The answers state that [automation of the health offices is under implementation](<https://www.emro.who.int/images/stories/crvs/documents/egypt.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system, and the source's latest year is 2011. Establishing would need a national system that takes the clinics' reports, keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms.

No stage is set. The joint external evaluation of August 2025 recommended a [USSD-based national electronic reporting system](<https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/1c6a1499-7f49-4b88-930a-a83b18c5d55e/content>) and a [mobile-based data system for essential health service use during emergencies](<https://iris.who.int/server/api/core/bitstreams/1c6a1499-7f49-4b88-930a-a83b18c5d55e/content>). The Ministry of Health has a [DHIS2 tracker program](<https://community.dhis2.org/t/overcoming-connectivity-barriers-the-role-of-dhis2-platform-in-enhancing-health-data-management-in-eritrea/57621>), and [Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR)](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2023-02/WHO%20Annual%20Report%20-%202022.pdf>) serves one function. No electronic medical record has been found at any tier. No dated statement that patient records are on paper at every tier has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need electronic patient records in use in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system procured or being prepared.

The sector plan HSSDP III, dated October 2021, states that [DHIS2 had been rolled out to about 40 per cent of facilities at secondary level and above](<https://extranet.who.int/cpcd/sites/default/files/public_file_repository/ERI_Eritrea_Health%20Sector%20Strategic%20and%20Development%20Plan%20%28HSSDP%20III%29_2022-2026.pdf>). WHO Eritrea reported in 2022 [a functional DHIS-2 at national level, at sub-national level and in 44% of the districts](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2023-02/WHO%20Annual%20Report%20-%202022.pdf>). A DHIS2 Community post of March 2024 describes the flow. [Data enters the national DHIS2 from zones and sub-zones over the ministry's local networks, running offline](<https://community.dhis2.org/t/overcoming-connectivity-barriers-the-role-of-dhis2-platform-in-enhancing-health-data-management-in-eritrea/57621>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No primary clinic has been found entering its own reports, and no share or count of clinics has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

The Ministry of Health stated in December 2024 that [electronic medical records were introduced in over 70 health facilities](<https://www.moh.gov.et/sites/default/files/2024-12/REQUEST%20OF%20EXPRESSION%20OF%20INTEREST%20.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 23 December 2025, Ethiopia and the United States [signed the memorandum](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-0004QN-Ethiopia-Health-12.23.2025.pdf>). It [schedules a national multi-tenant EMR](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-0004QN-Ethiopia-Health-12.23.2025.pdf>), with piloting in 2026, 48 facilities by 2027 and 438 by 2030. Its baseline is [0% of hospitals and health centres implementing the full national EMR](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-0004QN-Ethiopia-Health-12.23.2025.pdf>). No source gives the tier of the 70-plus facilities or the total they are drawn from. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

On 23 December 2025 Ethiopia signed a memorandum with the United States that [names DHIS2 as the country's HMIS](<https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/2026-0004QN-Ethiopia-Health-12.23.2025.pdf>). Interviews from October 2023 to March 2024 found that [health information technicians key routine reports into DHIS2 at their own facilities](<https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0314505>). Health posts [record largely on paper and send monthly to their health centre](<https://www.joghr.org/article/75141->), as surveyed in 2019 and 2020. A 2025 study puts [over 4,000 primary health care institutions, 95% of those eligible, on DHIS2](<https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13690-025-01641-0>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. That 95% counts institutions of all kinds, and no share of primary clinics alone has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

On 11 February 2026 the health information system eGabon-SIS [worked in 13 pilot sites across Grand Libreville](<https://gabonactu.com/blog/2026/02/11/projet-egabon-sis-la-banque-mondiale-satisfaite-du-bon-fonctionnement-du-systeme-dans-les-hopitaux-pilotes/>), on Gabonactu's account. The Libreville university hospital and the regional hospitals were not yet covered. In the last twelve months, the World Bank project [was officially closed on 24 June 2026](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-sante-cloture-du-projet-egabon-sis/>). [The Sino-Gabonese Cooperation Hospital went live on 13 July 2026](<https://gabonmediatime.com/egabon-sis-la-digitalisation-effective-a-lhopital-de-la-cooperation-sino-gabonaise/>). No count of primary clinics using the system, and no denominator, has been found. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

DHIS2 was [launched nationally on 6 December 2024](<https://hisprwanda.org/dhis2-officially-launched-in-gabon-hisp-rwandas-pivotal-role-in-transforming-health-information-management/>), as HISP Rwanda reported. WHO Gabon says it [integrated all functional public health facilities](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2025-07/Annual%20Report%202024%20Verso%20V.Final_.pdf>) and trained [122 data managers and 10 regional health directors](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2025-07/Annual%20Report%202024%20Verso%20V.Final_.pdf>) in 2024. In the last twelve months, [in June 2026 data managers of the Libreville region's university hospitals were trained to send data through DHIS2](<https://sante.gouv.ga/renforcement-des-capacites-en-gestion-des-donnees-sanitaires-les-majors-et-gestionnaires-de-donnees-formes-a-lutilisation-du-dhis2/>). No source names the tiers that report. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

In the last twelve months, a Ghana Medical Journal editorial of January 2026 [says the ministry discontinued LHIMS after its contract expired in December 2024](<https://doi.org/10.4314/gmj.v59i4.1>). No source shows which tiers or how many facilities use GHIMS. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

The Ghana Health Service's strategy for 2023-2027 [lists DHIMS II first among its digital health solutions](<https://ghs.gov.gh/api/media/file/POLICY_AND_STRATEGY_ON_DIGITAL_HEALTH-2.pdf>). The Ministry of Health's plan of June 2022 states that [most facilities validate and enter their data into DHIMS2 themselves](<https://www.moh.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/HISSP_2022-2025_FINALVERSION-1.pdf>). In March 2024, CHPS staff in three Northern Region districts said [their compounds lacked login details and computers](<https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0341176>). Paper reports [went to the sub-district or the district office for upload](<https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0341176>). In the last twelve months, [in November 2026 the Health Minister directed that DHIMS be joined to GHIMS](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/health-minister-directs-integration-of-dhims-and-ghims-to-unify-health-data-systems/>), the hospital system. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

A ministry mission of 17 to 22 August 2026 [reviewed five digitised facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts running OpenClinic](<https://lepandaguinee.com/2026/08/26/guinee-a-mamou-et-dalaba-le-pari-de-la-reforme-sanitaire-prend-une-nouvelle-dimension/>). In the last twelve months, the Dalaba prefectural hospital [deployed OpenClinic in January 2026](<https://lepandaguinee.com/2026/08/26/guinee-a-mamou-et-dalaba-le-pari-de-la-reforme-sanitaire-prend-une-nouvelle-dimension/>). In March 2026 the Swiss Re Foundation had the Clinic+O record [in use in rural communities and at Community Health Centers](<https://www.swissrefoundation.org/what-we-do/projects/access-to-health/Clinic-O--Strengthening-community-based-primary-healthcare-in-rural-Guinea.html>). No count of hospitals has been found against which these figures can be set. No count or district has been found for health centres using Clinic+O. Its PASA2 page of 2025 states that [health posts, health centres and prefectural hospitals collect SNIS data on paper primary tools](<https://pasa2.sante.gov.gn/activite-cle/gestion-analyse-et-validation-des-donnees-snis-dhis2/>). The data are keyed into DHIS2. In the last twelve months the SNIS [reached what the ministry calls a historic record of 100% completeness](<https://sante.gov.gn/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Bulletin_Performance_Sanitaire_N1_T1_28052026.pdf>). No share or count of centres or posts entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

The National Health Sector Policy of February 2024 states that the health sector [does not have a robust electronic medical record system in place](<https://moh.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FINAL-NATIONAL-HEALTH-POLICY_28-FEB-2024.pdf>). The World Bank's identity diagnostic of 2025 says a health information system is [managing patient records and issuing health cards](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102025103014657/pdf/P502279-e8627dee-4568-45e7-bb51-9a1aea1ff040.pdf>), and names no facility. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source shows whether either pilot was running at 30 September 2026. Establishing would need electronic patient records in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts.

It [places the electronic HMIS at the seven regional health directorates and the ministry](<https://moh.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FINAL-NATIONAL-HEALTH-POLICY_28-FEB-2024.pdf>). At the facility the HMIS is [paper, in registers and monthly return forms](<https://moh.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/FINAL-NATIONAL-HEALTH-POLICY_28-FEB-2024.pdf>). A tuberculosis pilot at 11 sites between June and November 2024 saw the sites [kept generating their monthly reports for the DHIS2 aggregate system from paper registers](<https://journals.theunion.org/content/ijtldo/3/3/138.full.pdf>). Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

No stage is set. As at June 2023, the one electronic patient record found is at a single private clinic in Bissau, and no source states its tier. INASA's 2022 yearbook tabulates [the monthly reports of health centres entered in DHIS2](<https://www.afro.who.int/sites/default/files/2024-05/Anu%C3%A1rio%20estat%C3%ADstico%202022_web.pdf>), 1,747 of 2,073 expected. In the last twelve months, on 6 October 2026, the DHIS2 project announced [an agreement to support INASA on the national system's data quality](<https://dhis2.org/hisp-to-strengthen-guinea-bissaus-national-dhis2-system/>). It brings [new HIV and tuberculosis patient-tracking tools](<https://dhis2.org/hisp-to-strengthen-guinea-bissaus-national-dhis2-system/>). No number or share of health centres keying their own reports has been found. No fact on tablet entry follows the 2018 pilot. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

EHAS states that elsewhere [health facilities filled paper register sheets](<https://ehas.org/que-hacemos/sis/sis-guinea-ecuatorial/>), which ministry staff transferred to spreadsheets. In a memorandum of 9 December 2025 with the United States, Liberia [commits to an open-source EMR in clinics, health centers and hospitals](<https://healthpolicy-watch.news/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/US-Liberia-MOU-2025.pdf>). No national figure for clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility.

Libya Herald reported in May 2022 that [the trial operation of the system was inaugurated](<https://libyaherald.com/2022/05/trail-run-of-the-unified-electronic-health-file-system-inaugurated/>) at two clinics, in Tripoli and Benghazi. In the last twelve months, in February 2026, the ministry [launched the National Digital Health Policy (2026-2036)](<https://www.afro.who.int/countries/namibia/news/namibia-launches-national-digital-health-policy-advance-equitable-people-centred-healthcare>). No count of centres keying their own reports has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics entering their own reports at the facility.

The counts cover facilities of all types, not primary clinics alone. No record retrievable at another facility has been found. Operating would need more than half of primary clinics keeping electronic records, each retrievable at another facility.

The U.S. President's Malaria Initiative's profile, published in 2023, [describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health and Child Care's system, to which donors and partners have very limited access](<https://mesamalaria.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ZIMZABWE-Malaria-Profile-PMI-FY-2024.pdf>). It states that [monthly collection is on paper at village, health facility and hospital levels](<https://mesamalaria.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ZIMZABWE-Malaria-Profile-PMI-FY-2024.pdf>). The district health information officer enters the paper records into DHIS2. The profile's routine table [gives 1,776 health facilities reporting into the HMIS/DHIS2 in 2022](<https://mesamalaria.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/ZIMZABWE-Malaria-Profile-PMI-FY-2024.pdf>). In the last twelve months, the Countdown to 2030 synthesis report states that [the national reporting rate of health facility data in DHIS2 was above 92% in 2024](<https://www.countdown2030.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Zimbabwe-Synthesis-Report.pdf>). No count of primary clinics entering their own reports has been found. Operating would need a published share or count showing that more than half of primary clinics enter their own reports.
